newsitem.title: FINLAND: ILKKA SEES LOWER TRADING IMPACT IN 97.
newsitem.headline: ILKKA SEES LOWER TRADING IMPACT IN 97.

text.p: Finnish media group Ilkka Oy said on Tuesday it expected lower securities trading volumes this year to hit net sales and earnings, and the result would be burdened by a fall in interest revenues and start-up costs.

"Group net sales are expected to fall compared to 1996 mainly due to decreasing volume in securities trading. The lower volume will also for its part affect group earnings," it said in a statement with its January-April report.
It said a newspaper plant project was proceeding according to plan, but would burden this year's earnings.

"The current year will be burdened by the additional personnel needs related to the start-up, installation and ramp-up phase of the newspaper plant, as well as by increased materials consumption in the testing period," Ilkka said.
"A fall in net interest revenues due to financing of the newspaper plant will also burden 1997 earnings," it said.

Ilkka reported January-April profit before extraordinary items down to 7.7 million markka from 11.7 million in the year-ago period. Its full-year 1996 profit before extraordinary items was 32.8 million markka.
